Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

sampling context together.

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Directly transferable nucleoside-analog contexts show measured oral F above 20%: zalcitabine ~80% in fasted patients (C29), didanosine fasting F 0.22–0.28 (C08, C14), zidovudine F 0.61±0.22 in cirrhosis (C10), zalcitabine 30% in fasted mice (C62), didanosine 42% (C45), and children mean F 0.27±0.13 (C68).

L3 oral exposure records for structurally similar ribonucleosides show substantial systemic exposure after oral dosing, e.g., ribavirin AUC0-12 3325.83 ng·h/mL and Tmax 1.61 h (C92, C82), and lamivudine 300 mg AUC0-inf 13.2 µg·h/mL and Cmax 3.3 µg/mL (C100, C119).
L4 shows high solubility for the closely related ribavirin across physiological pH (C141, C133, C138), supporting a favorable dissolution component for this polar nucleoside class.

L4 also shows low Caco-2/PAMPA permeability for ribavirin (C134, C139, C143), levovirin (C160, C148), didanosine (C153), and gemcitabine (C150, C135, C158), but low passive permeability is not affirmative low-F evidence: didanosine has measured F ~22–42% despite low PAMPA, and ribavirin's low Caco-2 value is attributed to limited hCNT2 expression (C134), not necessarily poor in vivo absorption.
The only sub-20% nucleoside F record, gemcitabine in mice (C47), is low-transferability and reflects a different metabolic liability; it does not overturn the high prediction for AICAR.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for AICAR/acadesine is present in the supplied records.

L4 permeability assays are in vitro and may underrepresent nucleoside transporter-mediated absorption, e.g., hCNT2.
No AICAR-specific first-pass metabolism or clearance data are available.
Analog oral F values are variable, so population-level inference is uncertain.
